faq.q: How do I compare the time in two cities?
faq.a: Add the cities with the search box and the time grid shows every hour side by side, with the live offset between them.

faq.q: Does WorldTime handle daylight saving time?
faq.a: Yes. Daylight saving transitions are detected automatically for each city, so the offset is correct on spring-forward and fall-back days too.

faq.q: How do I find the best time for an international meeting?
faq.a: Add everyone's cities, then use the color heatmap to find hours where no one is asleep. Select a slot to export it to your calendar.
Yes, WorldTime is completely free, runs in the browser, and does not require an account.

faq.q: Is the time shown in real time?
faq.a: The current time and converter tables update live in your browser every minute.

About.title: About WorldTime
About.metaDescription: How WorldTime calculates local time, offsets, and daylight saving from IANA — plus features and use cases.
About.lead: WorldTime is a free world clock, time-zone converter, and meeting planner. It is built for reading overlap at a glance — no account, no paywall.
About.howBody: Each city is mapped to one IANA time zone. Offsets and calendar dates are computed with Luxon from that zone at a given instant, in the browser and in the HTML we send to crawlers.
About.dataBody: Zone rules come from the IANA Time Zone Database (tzdb), the same dataset used by operating systems. We do not scrape other clock websites.
About.dstBody: DST is taken from the zone, not from a URL label. A slug like EST--PST is a search alias; in summer America/New_York is EDT. The live abbreviation on each page is authoritative.
About.shareBody: A selection you make is encoded in the page URL. When you share a link, you share the cities and the highlighted time window — nothing else. There are no accounts, and visitors never see each other's data.
About.offlineBody: WorldTime is a Progressive Web App. If you install it, a service worker caches pages on your device so the app keeps working offline. The cache never leaves your device.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.metaDescription: Privacy policy: no account, no ads, no analytics. Your cities and settings stay in your browser; sharing happens through the link itself.
Privacy.lead: WorldTime is a no-account utility. This page explains, in plain language, what little data is involved and where it lives.

sections.heading: The short version
paragraphs: You do not need an account, and the clock has no user database. We do not ask for your name, email, or phone number, and we do not sell personal data.

sections.heading: Data stored on your device
paragraphs: The cities you add, your home city, hour format, working-hours settings, your current selection, and your theme preference are stored in your browser's local storage so the grid can restore on your next visit.
This data stays on your device. Clearing the site data in your browser removes all of it.

sections.heading: Links you share
paragraphs: When you copy or share a link, your cities and time selection are encoded in the URL itself — that is how sharing works without a server-side account.
Anyone with the link can view those cities and that time window. The URL contains no other personal data.

sections.heading: Cookies
paragraphs: WorldTime shows no ads, embeds no analytics, and includes no third-party trackers.

The only cookie you may receive is NEXT_LOCALE, a small technical cookie that remembers your language choice between visits. It contains no personal identifiers, and you can remove it by clearing cookies for this site.

sections.heading: Server requests and logs
paragraphs: Like every website, your browser requests pages from our hosting. For security and abuse prevention, the hosting layer may keep short-lived technical logs, such as IP address, browser type, and request time.
We do not use these logs to build user profiles, and we do not sell or share them for advertising.

sections.heading: Offline cache (PWA)
paragraphs: If you install WorldTime as an app, a service worker caches pages on your device for offline use. The cache stays on that device only.

sections.heading: Children
paragraphs: WorldTime is a general-audience tool. We knowingly collect no personal data from anyone, including children.

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: If this page changes, we will update the date at the top. Continued use of the site after a change means you accept the current version.

Terms.title: Terms of Service
Terms.metaDescription: Terms of service: WorldTime is free and provided as-is; time data is for reference — verify critical deadlines independently.
Terms.lead: These terms cover your use of WorldTime. The short version: it is a free tool, provided as-is; double-check anything that really matters.

sections.heading: Accepting these terms
paragraphs: By using WorldTime you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the service.

sections.heading: What the service is
paragraphs: WorldTime is a free world clock, time-zone converter, and meeting planner. It requires no account and has no paid tier.
We may add, change, or remove features at any time. The About and FAQ pages describe how the current version works.

sections.heading: Fair use
paragraphs: Please use the site lawfully, and do not attempt to disrupt, overload, or circumvent its normal operation. Automated access that harms the service for other visitors is not allowed.

sections.heading: Accuracy of time data
paragraphs: Times, offsets, and daylight-saving rules are computed from the IANA Time Zone Database. The data is widely trusted, but time-zone rules change with legislation, and edge cases exist.
Do not rely on WorldTime alone for critical deadlines, legal cutoffs, or last-minute meetings. Verify important times with an authoritative source.

sections.heading: No warranty

sections.heading: Limitation of liability

sections.heading: Content and intellectual property
paragraphs: The WorldTime name, interface, code, and written content belong to this project. Time-zone facts come from the public IANA database.
You are welcome to link to the site and to quote the times it shows.
